messages:
sam_ops: quick flag 26 files from last night's prod DB backup show empty SSE/KMS headers on head-object. spotted by random audit.
rita_sec: oof. bucket? example key?
sam_ops: s3://redwood-backups/prod/db/2026-12-05/snap-20261205-02.tar.gz
jon_db: that usually means multipart commit lost final metadata. any KMS grant activity?
encrypt-bot: [audit] query=service:backup-uploader AND time=2026-12-05 returned 187 events; grant G-20261205-11 issued ttl=90m expired during run.
kai_sre: timeline: backup 01:40-03:20, grant expired 02:45. uploader falls back to SSE-S3 but old multipart client sometimes omits SSE headers on complete.
rita_sec: action: 1) list objects in window and classify SSE: none/SSE-S3. 2) run copy->SSE-KMS for affected where perms allow. 3) extend grant TTL or issue renewals for long jobs. 4) change uploader to fail loudly on missing CMEK.
sam_ops: running a quick scan now, pushing results to #eng-security-private.
jon_db: note: copy-object with --sse aws:kms will re-encrypt in-place (server-side copy). ensure copier role has kms:Encrypt/Decrypt.
kai_sre: I'll add a post-upload head-object check and a preflight KMS-grant assert. Also open infra ticket for copier perms.
sam_ops: start re-encrypt batch now; will report failures if any AccessDenied.
